messages.body_plain:
Hi Bernd,
I gave your code a go for converting my genlight object (nematode with 395 loci, 3.17% missing data) into a format useable by the package related. As far as I can tell it works well.

The only strange thing about my results is Wang's estimate results in values of -1.x when a certain individual is part of the dyad. Looking at the gtd matrix doesn't provide any clues as to what is different about this individual. Anyway, I am assuming that this is a problem with my data and not the conversion.

Thanks for the handy code.
Cheers,
Bonnie

>
>
>
>

>
>
>
>

>
>
>
>
>
>
>

> library(related)

>
>
>

>
>

> mm <- ifelse(mm==1,0,mm)
>
>
>
> mm[, seq(2,nLoc(x)*2,2)] <- gd
>
> mm <- ifelse(mm==1,2,mm)
>
>
>
> mm <- mm+1
>
> mm <- ifelse(is.na <http://is.na>(mm),0,mm)
>
>
>
> gtd <- data.frame(V1=as.character(indNames(x)), mm)
>
> gtd$V1 <- as.character(gtd$V1)
>
>
>
> #export as file
>
> #write.table(gtd, file = "gtd.txt", sep = "\t",col.names = F, row.names = F)

> #load from file
>
> #gtd <- readgenotypedata("gtd.txt")$gdata
>
>
>
> #---Calculate Relatedness---#
>
> output <- coancestry(gtd, lynchrd=2, quellergt=2, wang=2)
>
>
>
> #---View Point Estimates---#
>
> output$relatedness

messages.body_plain:
Further to our previous announcement on the upgrade, we would like to elaborate:

(a) dartR has been upgraded to accommodate SilicoDArT data, that is, the presence or absence of sequence tags called or not called, as well as the SNP genotype data. There are analyses that cannot be done on tag P/A data, and the scripts trap that. Both forms of data are stored as genlight objects (read in by gl.read.dart and gl.read.silicodart respectively), the distinction being whether the ploidy is 2 (SNP data) or ploidy is 1 (Tag P/A data).

(b) A computational efficiency has been built in to avoid recalculating stats unnecessarily, which is embedded in the genlight objects. This may require you to run gl <- gl.compatability.check(gl) to avoid throwing errors.

(c) The pcoa scripts have been substantially rewritten to distinguish between PCA (SNP or SilicoDArT data as input, covariance matrix based computations) and PCoA (distance matrix input, any distance measure pretty much). Distortions that may arise (manifested as negative eigenvalues in the noise dimensions) from using a sparse matrix (lots of NAs) or non-metric distance measures can be accommodated by applying recognised transformations (sensu ape).

(d) The scripts for fixed differences have been amended to allow greater control and more diagnostics (using gl.collapse repeatedly), though gl.collapse.recursive still works.

(e) A novel approach to standardizing heterozygosity across species and studies has been introduced. Not a panacea, but worth examination. Use gl.report.secondaries to estimate the number of sequence tags with no snps, and use this value in gl.report.heterozygosity (as n.invariant).

There have been some bug fixes, but software development has a problem of reaching a steady state where bugs are removed but new bugs are created at the same rate. Hence the beta release.

Please pipe up with issues.

I found this 2018 paper to be helpful: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/29160928

Bonnie
